This is notebook is showcasing how to determine a narcissistic number in both Python and R

```{python}
def narc_num(x):
  digits = [int(n) for n in str(x)]
  #First we turn x into a string, then we loop through each character in the string
  #then turn each character back into an integer and add it to a list.
  i = 0
  j = len(digits)
  #J is the number of digits x has (100 has 3 digits for example)
  for i in range(j):
    digits[i] = digits[i]**j
    # Now we raise that number in the list to the power based on how many digits 
    # there are (1^3 for 100 for example)
  if sum(digits) == x:
    return(True)
  else:
    return(False)
```

```{r}
library(stringr)
narcnum <- function(x){
  digi <- c()
  #Create a blank vector
  i = 1
  j <- nchar(x)
  #J is the number of digits x has (100 has 3 digits for example)
  for(i in 1:j){
    s <- (x%/%10^(i-1))%%10
    #S starts by finding what value is in each place value (0 is in the ones for
    #a hundred and for the tens as well for example)
    s <- s^j
    #Then we raise that number to the power based on how many digits there are
    #(1^3 for 100 for example)
    digi <- append(digi,s)
    #Add that value into the vector
  }
  summ <- sum(digi)
  #Now lets find the sum of the vector
  if(summ == x){
    return(TRUE)
  }else{
    return(FALSE)
  }
}
```
